messages:
Maya Patel: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands pricing slide — can someone clarify how the new granular throttles interact with bundle credits? e.g., if a customer has a 1M token/month bundle but we're enforcing per-route throttles, do throttled requests still consume bundle tokens or are they queued/dropped before billing?
Sanjay Rao: short answer: throttles are enforcement, billing counts executed requests only. If we drop a request (429), nothing consumes the customer's bundle. If we queue and it eventually executes, it consumes tokens.
Maya Patel: thanks — what's the behavior for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity? any different accounting?
Sanjay Rao: Dedicated customers with reserved capacity still bill on execution. But we have an internal policy: reserved capacity commitments include a baseline of tokens (commit), which is reconciled monthly. Overages are charged from bundle or overage pricing depending on contract.
Emily Rivera: to add: for committed Dedicated plans we prorate monthly baseline usage against the commit. Bundles are used to offset overages only if the contract links a bundle SKU — we have a mapping table in Billing (link below).
Olivia Chen: from runtime side: throttles run at the routing layer. Implementation: per-route limiter runs before batching/cache. If request is rejected at that layer it never hits the serving runtime and thus doesn't increment token counters. Here's the quick pseudo-config we use in prod:
```
rate_limit:
  scope: route
  window_ms: 1000
  max_tokens: 50
```
Chris Gomez: practical question — how should support respond when a customer reports "I'm getting 429s but my dashboard shows tokens still dropping"? I've seen this confusion with multi-route apps.
Olivia Chen: likely they're looking at aggregate token drains from background retries or fallback routes that executed. Ask them to provide route + trace id. We also plan a dashboard change to show per-route attempted vs executed tokens.
billing-bot: Billing doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/granular-throttles — updated mapping table v3. (automated)
Maya Patel: roadmap question: is there an explicit product change planned to let customers choose whether throttled-but-queued requests consume bundle tokens? that was asked during demo.
Sanjay Rao: yes — on roadmap: "throttle semantics toggle" in Q3. It'll be a per-tenant flag: drop-before-bill (default), queued-then-bill (opt-in). We'll expose via Console + API. I'll post the RFC next week.
Maya Patel: perfect. please add a short blurb for sales and CSMs so we don't overpromise. cc @Chris Gomez
Chris Gomez: will do — I'll draft a canned reply template and share in #support later today :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: thanks everyone — closing the loop.
